recipes.name: Spinach Basil Pasta Salad
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Add bow tie pasta and return to a boil. Cook, uncovered and stirring occasionally, until pasta has cooked through but is still firm to the bite, about 12 minutes. Rinse with cold water to cool, then drain well in a colander set in the sink.
Toss spinach and basil together in a large bowl.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add garlic and sauté for 1 minute. Stir in prosciutto and cook 2 to 3 minutes more. Remove from the heat.
Add prosciutto mixture to spinach and basil and toss to combine. Pour in the drained pasta and toss again. Season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and pine nuts to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach Basil Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: Perfect for summer, this fresh spinach and basil pasta salad features nutty Parmesan, toasted pine nuts, and little bits of salty prosciutto.

video.description: A delicious mix of fresh spinach and pasta tossed with olive oil, garlic, and prosciutto.

review.reviewBody: This is my new favorite salad -- used all spinach instead of basil and used fried choped up bacon instead of prosciutto -- You never can go wrong with bacon -- there is never any left over and I always have left over pasta salad. You can leave out the nuts and it is still wonderful.

We just tried this tonight. My 11 year old asked when we could have it again. My 14 year old ate three helpings. We loved the flavors and I loved how simple and easy this was to throw together. I served it warm and thought it was great. I cut the oil to 1/4 of a cup and that was more than enough for us. I mixed the basil, spinach, garlic, prosciutto, and oil together and then poured the warm pasta over it and mixed that all together. Then I put a towel over the bowl and let the pasta wilt the spinach and basil a bit. Will definitely be making this again.

The whole basil leaves are just too strong for our taste. I would change it up by using less, and slicing them up into strips. This would allow a basil flavor without overpowering the dish. I would also cook and spinach and basil for a minute or two instead of just relying on the hot oil mixture to wilt it.

I really loved this dish! I did bacon instead of prosciutto and added sliced grape tomatoes that I cooked in the same pot as the sautéd garlic. I also added some bacon grease with the olive oil in the step mentioned above.

This is now a go to receipe!!! No one complains, I use 1lb of trimmed bacon. I snip the bacon and ditch the fattiest bits, fry it then drain on towels, drain the pan and then dump in the tomatoes, garlic....then put the bacon back in. Then put the spinach on top. I tried the spinach with the pasta water but it was a mess for me so I just load it on top of the tomato bacon stuff and put the lid on the pan....Kids prefer with parmesean, Husband and I prefer feta. I've also added marinated artichokes and mushrooms. The possibilities are endless with this one.! Prefer penne pasta per the recipe and some nice crusty warm bread. This is a great weekday meal!
Loved this. Did not need the whole box of pasta. Next time I will try with arugula. Had with grilled shrimp.

I have made this many times over the years..I have served it piping hot, room temperature and cold. I have added sun dried tomatoes in place of prosciutto and I often use walnuts in place of pignolis. Tonight I am making it with sliced grilled turkey sausage, peppers and vidalia onions. I will probably throw them all together. It's always a favorite. Thank you!

Delicious recipe! I added some grilled chicken & served this to my family as a one-dish meal tonight - they loved it & asked me to make it again...often! Made a few minor changes, improvising with the ingredients I had on hand - I used about half of the olive oil called for, substituted the prosciutto for 2 pieces of bacon and added some sauteed onions & little cream before tossing all together. Also I had to skip the Parmesan cheese, but I'm sure that would have made it even better!

This salad is fantastic! I've made it twice and each time have received so many compliments. I did switch to slivered almonds (toasted) and turkey bacon. The cook time for the turkey bacon was longer than 2-3 minutes- closer to 8-10 and it was tough to keep the garlic from getting to dark. But the garlic did get so nicely browned that it crumbled apart in your mouth in the salad- so delicious. Great recipe- thanks Jennifer!

Just added some sun dried and fresh tomatoes. Brought this to a picnic. Put the Parmesan in at home but saved the pine nuts and some extra basil to add just before serving as both are affected by being in moisture too long. This was a hit.

LOVE this! I did make some changes though so I can't give it 5 stars. I used bacon (never have prosciutto) and omitted the parm and pine nuts. The first time I made it the garlic was burned so I wouldn't saute it as long as it says. Also, it needs a bit of acid so I added halved cherry tomatoes and it was amazing. Definitely one of my favorites
Fantastic! I use Orecchiette (I found it at the store and had never had it) and it was GREAT!

THIS is the best pasta salad I've ever made! I make it EXACTLY to the recipe and everyone who has it, loves it - even kids as young as 4 - and every adult asks for the recipe!! THANK YOU SO MUCH FOR SHARING!!!
Beautiful and so delicious!
easy & quick to make. We enjoyed it.
My entire family loved this! Followed the recipe except we “accidentally” doubled the garlic. Yum!
Really good. Made it as written.
I added onions, tomato and more bacon. Ate it while still hot, was good.

I never write reviews but this was just too good not to comment! I made it exactly as written, and not only was it delicious but it looked beautiful too. I didn’t measure the basil, so I probably didn’t use the full amount, but I definitely wouldn’t skip it, as it adds a very distinct flavor. As other reviewers pointed out, it’s not a cheap salad, but it makes enough to feed a big crowd. Also, unlike many green salads, it’s not a bad leftover the next day. Enjoy!
This is fabulous!
